Finalize the book in [`docs/book/`](../../../docs/book), following the [book guide](book-guide.md).

Private comparison repositories (scan only, never written anywhere): `${input:comparisonPath:absolute path to the private comparison repositories}`.

## 1. Completeness

Check every file in the guide's output table. Report missing chapters and stop if any are missing, recommending `/book-next`.

## 2. `docs/book/README.md`

Write the title page:
- Title and subtitle (refine the working title if the chapters suggest a better one), author placeholder, and license note (the book is part of the Apache-2.0 repository; quoted Godot code is MIT with attribution).
- A one-page preface: who the book is for, what readers will learn, which tools and versions it was written against (VS Code version, GitHub Copilot, Claude Opus 5.5 and other frontier models, Godot version from `GODOT_VERSION`, Julia version from the README).
- A table of contents with a one-sentence summary for each chapter.
- "How this book was written": the book itself was generated by the prompts in [`.github/prompts/book/`](.), using the same resumable pattern as the implementation. List the prompts and how to re-run them.
- Prerequisites for the "Try it yourself" exercises (link to the repository README).

## 3. Consistency Pass

- Navigation lines are correct in every chapter (previous / contents / next).
- Terminology is uniform: "the agent", "parity matrix", "phase prompt", "ADR", built-in agent names and harness names as verified in chapter 2, `GodotObject`, `@godot_class`.
- Cross-references between chapters (for example chapters 7 ↔ 10 on `WeakRef` shadowing, 10 ↔ 15 on `NOTIFICATION_POSTINITIALIZE`, 3 ↔ 18 on parity tags) exist in both directions.
- No two chapters contradict each other on numbers or statuses. The parity matrix is the source of truth.
- The "Techniques to reuse" lists don't repeat the same technique under different names. Merge duplicates and point back to the chapter that introduces each technique.

## 4. Fact and Link Check

- Every relative link resolves to an existing file (use file search). Fix or remove broken links.
- Spot-check at least two numeric claims per chapter against their sources.
- Check that every quoted prompt matches the current file in `.github/prompts/` exactly. If a prompt changed after its chapter was written, update the quote and the analysis.

## Confidentiality Scan

Run this scan whenever a chapter mentions the comparison portfolio, and always as part of finalization. Do not write any of the scan terms to any file, todo list or memory, and do not echo them in chat.

1. Using read-only listing, collect the top-level directory names under the comparison path, plus the path itself and its final segment.
2. Derive search terms in working memory: each full directory name, and each distinctive component when names are split on `-`, `_`, `.`, and case changes. Ignore generic English or technology words that also appear naturally in this repository (for example "core", "test", "docs", "build", "main").
3. Search every file in `docs/book/` and `.github/prompts/book/`: case-insensitive for terms of 4 or more characters, and case-sensitive whole-word for shorter terms.
4. Also search for leak patterns: drive-letter paths outside this repository, e-mail addresses, internal-looking hostnames or URLs, and domain-specific terminology picked up from the portfolio.
5. Rewrite every hit as an anonymized, category-level statement, then re-run the scan until it is clean.
6. Report only "confidentiality scan passed" and the number of fixes made.

## 5. Report

Summarize: chapters and total word count, fixes made in each pass, open questions for the author (claims that could not be verified and were removed or softened), and the confidentiality scan result.
